svg.title: Where a prompt-heavy request waits in llm-d P/D on H100 at block 64
svg.desc: Animated path of one prompt-heavy request through llm-d prefill/decode disaggregation on H100 (2 prefill TP1 pods, 1 decode TP2 pod, block 64, concurrency 256): client, EPP router, routing sidecar on the decode pod, prefill queue (4,778 ms), prefill compute (359 ms), NIXL KV pull over NVLink (27 ms), decode queue (52 ms), then decode steps streaming tokens every 15.9 ms. Router plus sidecar plus network adds 50 ms. At the default block 16 the same setup and load spend 351 ms in the NIXL transfer and 2,183 ms in the decode queue, with ITL 60.6 ms. A to-scale bar shows the prefill queue dominating time to first token.
svg.text: At block 64 the KV transfer takes 27 ms, so the wait moves to the prefill queue (86% of TTFT)
Same setup as the block-size figure, at block 64: 2P (TP1) : 1D (TP2), ISL 4000 / OSL 200, c=256. Block 16: NIXL 351 ms, ITL 60.6 ms.
output tokens stream back to the client: one every 15.9 ms (ITL, server)

svg.text: Then one token every 15.9 ms. The bar sums the 5 layers (5,265 ms); about 288 ms of the 5,553 ms client TTFT is not attributed to a layer.
